problem: The first term of a geometric sequence is $\frac{5}{3}$ and the common ratio is $\frac{4}{3}.$ Written in sigma notation, what is the sum of the first $25$ terms?
worked_solution:
First, we must express the series in the form:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ denotes the first term of the series, $r$ denotes the common ratio, and $N$ denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, ${a}_{1}=\frac{5}{3},$ $r=\frac{4}{3}$ and $N=25.$

Expressing the geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain:

$$
{S}_{25}={\sum }_{n=1}^{25}\frac{5}{3}\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{n-1}\,\,
$$

Finally, we can simplify the above using the laws of exponents, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{25}\frac{5}{3}\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{n-1} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{25}\frac{5}{3}\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{n}\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{25}\frac{5}{3}\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{-1}\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{25}\frac{5}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{4}\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{25}\frac{5}{4}{(\frac{4}{3})}^{n}\end{aligned}
$$
